scenes.title: Zoo Scene 4 — Different Animal Habitats
scenes.brief: Compare where different zoo animals live, stand and swim.
targetExamples: The bear is near the cave.
The kangaroo is on the ground.
The otter is swimming in the water.

scenes.title: Zoo Scene 5 — Feeding Time
scenes.brief: Animal-care language, eating actions and feature comparison.
targetExamples: The giraffe is reaching for leaves.
The elephant is holding leaves with its trunk.
The zebra is standing in front.
The giraffe has a long neck.
The zebra is striped.

scenes.title: Zoo Scene 6 — Zoo Positions and Observation
scenes.brief: Spatial language, observation and simple inference in a zoo habitat.
targetExamples: The lion is on the rock.
The penguin is near the pool.
The monkey is climbing the frame.
The lion is above the penguin.

scenes.title: Zoo Scene 7 — Animals in Different Places
scenes.brief: Observe familiar zoo animals in places that suit them: by water, on a branch, or in shade.
targetExamples: The penguin is near the pool.
The lion is in the shade.
The monkey is on the branch.
The elephant is by the water.
The giraffe is tall.

scenes.title: Zoo Scene 8 — Animal Feature Clues
scenes.brief: Find animals from clues about their visible features and size.
targetExamples: The giraffe has a long neck.
The elephant is big and grey.
The lion has a mane.
The zebra is striped.
The penguin is small.

scenes.title: Zoo Scene 9 — Water, Shade and Rest
scenes.brief: Talk about what animals are doing and what they need in a warm zoo setting.
targetExamples: The elephant is near the water.
The lion is resting in the shade.
The penguin is by the pool.
The monkey is on the tree branch.
The animals look calm.

scenes.brief: Five different zoo-animal actions: spraying, eating leaves, walking, swimming and climbing.
One giraffe, elephant, lion, zebra and penguin with strong contrasts in height, size, colour and visible animal features.
targetExamples: The giraffe is tall.
The giraffe has a long neck.
The elephant is big and grey.
The elephant has a long trunk.
The lion has a big mane.
The zebra is striped.
The penguin is small.

scenes.brief: Six spatial examples in a wildlife park: on, near, behind, next to, under and between.
